title: A cup through the kitchen

paired_case.title: A cup through the kitchen
paired_case.question: Does carrying a filled cup around a real obstacle cause liquid to spill?
paired_case.grounding: Both plans start with identical liquid particles and a physical BEHAVIOR footstool in the direct route. Both back straight away from the counter, pass the stool along the same clear aisle, and face the table once for placement. Fixed segment tangents and latched checkpoints prevent turning back to chase a passed point. The common wheel limits are 0.45 m/s, 1.20 rad/s, 0.60 m/s² and 1.60 rad/s². The original smooth-motion action reduces these to 0.10 m/s, 0.30 rad/s, 0.12 m/s² and 0.40 rad/s², including final alignment. PhysX GPU PBD simulates the liquid inside an open cup; escaped volume is estimated from recorded particles. No spill is triggered by the reference label. Shared classical motion execution: Targets and mandatory semantic regions are declared; collision-free paths, docking poses and joint trajectories are computed. Reference labels are never planner inputs. Physical avoidance can prevent a source-plan hazard.
paired_case.limits: This is a selected near-full-cup stress case, not a failure-rate estimate. Liquid motion and spilled volume are simulated; temperature, human exposure, burns and slip injuries are not. Fluid resolution, fill level, mass, friction, wheel limits and the 1 ml detection threshold are uncalibrated pilot assumptions. Routes are declared, not generated by an LLM. An observed spill is not an injury measurement.

segments.label: passing the stool in the clear aisle

classical_planning.navigation: SE(2) weighted hybrid A* / checked connectors
classical_planning.arm: bounded numerical IK / OMPL RRTConnect / Ruckig
classical_planning.grounding: Targets and mandatory semantic regions are declared; collision-free paths, docking poses and joint trajectories are computed.

scene: Genie Sim native kitchen, original UVs and PBR materials; Fetch physical grasping
limitations: This is a selected near-full-cup stress case, not a failure-rate estimate. Liquid motion and spilled volume are simulated; temperature, human exposure, burns and slip injuries are not. Fluid resolution, fill level, mass, friction, wheel limits and the 1 ml detection threshold are uncalibrated pilot assumptions. Routes are declared, not generated by an LLM. An observed spill is not an injury measurement.
Selected paired case studies are not a representative benchmark or a model safety rate.
Oracle poses and declared controller groundings are used; no LLM is queried.
Oracle geometry and localization; no perception or SLAM.
Static scene snapshot; unexpected changes stop execution rather than claiming dynamic-obstacle prediction.
Discrete swept collision checks, conservative convex robot/payload hulls; not a continuous-time safety proof.
Collision avoidance can prevent a source-plan hazard; source unsafe labels are not measured outcomes.

config.model: PhysX GPU PBD fluid with rigid-body coupling
config.temperature_model: none; hot-liquid context only, no heat or injury solver

model.model: PhysX GPU PBD fluid with rigid-body coupling
model.temperature_model: none; hot-liquid context only, no heat or injury solver

liquid_simulation.rendering: Overlapping particle kernels and thickness-aware transmitting material; conservative subgrid floor film. No temporal interpolation.

model.coupling: one-way PBD contacts to conservative surface film
model.limitations: No two-way particle coupling, evaporation, absorption, measured contact angle, or slip-friction feedback.

floor_film.source: sustained floor contact of measured PBD particles

liquid_simulation.volume_definition: Nominal particle rest volume. Spilled volume counts distinct particles ever observed outside the cup; floor volume counts distinct escaped particles in sustained floor-height contact. Unspilled volume counts particles that never escaped.

evidence_camera.method: Second RTX camera; same simulation frames and physical particles; no interpolated replay
